parsed.explanation: Section 3 proves only that V cannot contain two distinct positive values. Nowhere does the text prove g(x) ≥ 0; the only constraint recorded is g(x) > -x (from positivity of f). The dichotomy (i)/(ii) therefore ignores the possibility of negative values of g (e.g. g taking values in a set containing a negative number and possibly 0 or one positive value). Sections 4–6 rely on V ⊆ {0, c} (every x in S_0 ∪ S_c), and Section 7's conclusion depends on it. The standard exclusion (iterating t, t+g(t), ... until it exits R_{>0} when g(t)<0) is not written anywhere. So the necessity argument is incomplete as stated; the objection correctly identifies the missing step.
